description:
FOUND s455 (Fable round-12 merge review) probing #755. REPRO (scratch q5.pl): touch "gx*wild.dat"; my @f = glob("gx*"); perl prints gx*wild.dat, PCL gx\*wild.dat. MECHANISM: %p-glob--expand-dir / the line-12408 collector render matched leaf names via file-namestring, which ESCAPES `*` `?` `[` `\`; %p-glob-leaf-name has the same rendering, and since the glob->regex FILTER runs over that escaped leaf, a wild-charactered name may also mis-MATCH, not just mis-print. FIX SHAPE: render leaf names the way %p-dirent-name now does (ea58eb4: cut from sb-ext:native-namestring, strip trailing slash) at every glob output/filter site; p-glob keeps its own wildcard parsing for the PATTERN (by design, #755). BAR: probe set = literal-wild names under patterns that match them (dotfile rule intact), Pl/t/glob-01.t + a new row, and the io/ companion leg if cl/ moves. PRE-EXISTING on 154f4a9 (probed in the AD worktree pre-merge).
--- DONE s456ah (Opus agent AH, round 13) ---
FIXED by DELETING the duplicate: %p-glob-leaf-name was a second copy of
%p-dirent-name built on file-namestring (which escapes `* ? [ \`), so it is
gone and its one caller -- plus the %p-glob--expand-pathname fallback, which
called file-namestring directly -- now use %p-dirent-name.  readdir and glob
share ONE literal leaf-name renderer.  p-glob keeps its own PATTERN wildcard
parsing (DECIDED s455).
The MATCHING half the filing suspected is real and was measured: the escaped
leaf is what the glob->regex filter scans, so glob("gx?q.dat") over a file
literally named gx?q.dat matched NOTHING, and only 3 of 8 returned names named
an existing file.  Probe set: 12 lines vs perl 5.40.3 -- 3 matched before, 11
after.  Guard Pl/t/wild-filename-01.t 11 -> 15 rows (its perl-oracle battery).
The 12th line is task #830 (the glob PATTERN has no backslash escape at all),
filed with its five-row probe table and the reason it is not a one-arm fix.
subject: glob() RESULTS escape wild characters in matched names: a file named gx*wild.dat globbed by gx* answers gx\*wild.dat (perl: gx*wild.dat) -- #755 family, OUTPUT side of the glob matcher
